profile.research_note: [batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This CyrusOne campus sits in Loudoun County, Virginia, in and around Sterling, part of the Northern Virginia Ashburn area data center corridor. Wikipedia coverage of CyrusOne states the company purchased 40 acres in Loudoun County in June 2016 for data center construction. CyrusOne was founded in July 2000 by David Ferdman and Larry Bursten, went public in 2013, and was taken private in 2022 when Kohlberg Kravis Roberts and Global Infrastructure Partners acquired it for 15 billion dollars. No building specific address or individual MW figures were located in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Sterling campus in Loudoun County publishes 116 MW of IT capacity across three facilities, equivalent to roughly 2,900 racks at typical AI training density and representing 8.4 percent of Virginia's total disclosed capacity.

The campus sits within the Ashburn corridor, a region that has consolidated Northern Virginia's power and fiber infrastructure since CyrusOne acquired 40 acres there in 2016. This geographic concentration reflects how data center operators cluster around existing grid and network assets rather than distributing capacity. The scale and location make this facility relevant to regional power constraints as AI workloads grow.

What the data does not disclose limits inference about current utilization. CyrusOne publishes no individual building breakdowns, power density figures, or workload mix for NVA5-NVA7. The operator does not state whether these 116 MW support training, inference, or both, nor how much capacity sits in use versus reserved. CyrusOne itself moved to private ownership under KKR and Global Infrastructure Partners in 2022, but no tenant information or pricing has entered the public record for this site.
